A double-buffering strategy to systematically overlap compute (LOD calculation, vertex assembly) and rendering passes by swapping front and back buffers between frames [S3].

The claim accurately reflects the content of Source [S3]. The source explicitly describes a 'double-buffering strategy' used to 'systematically overlap computation and rendering' by 'swapping buffer roles' (front and back buffers) between frames. It details that compute passes (LOD calculation, vertex assembly) write to the back buffer while the render pass uses the front buffer from the previous frame, which aligns perfectly with the claim.
